variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Object storage is a data architecture that stores a value as an object addressed by a bucket or container and a key, together with system and application metadata. Clients use an API to create, read, list, copy, version, and delete whole objects rather than mounting a general-purpose filesystem and mutating arbitrary byte ranges in place.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Bucket or container
pairs.detail: Groups a namespace under region, ownership, encryption, public-access, versioning, lifecycle, logging, and replication configuration.
pairs.explanation: Groups a namespace under region, ownership, encryption, public-access, versioning, lifecycle, logging, and replication configuration.

pairs.label: Object key
pairs.detail: Identifies the object within the bucket.
pairs.explanation: Identifies the object within the bucket. Prefixes can support listing and partitioning, but they are not automatically filesystem directories.

pairs.label: Version
pairs.detail: Distinguishes historical values or delete markers when versioning is enabled.
pairs.explanation: Distinguishes historical values or delete markers when versioning is enabled. Retention and lifecycle determine which versions survive.

pairs.label: Metadata and checksum
pairs.detail: Carries content type, schema, owner, tags, encryption state, source, and integrity evidence used by downstream consumers.
pairs.explanation: Carries content type, schema, owner, tags, encryption state, source, and integrity evidence used by downstream consumers.

variants.hint:
Bucket or container: Groups a namespace under region, ownership, encryption, public-access, versioning, lifecycle, logging, and replication configuration.

Object key: Identifies the object within the bucket.

Version: Distinguishes historical values or delete markers when versioning is enabled.

Metadata and checksum: Carries content type, schema, owner, tags, encryption state, source, and integrity evidence used by downstream consumers.
variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

variants.title: Give each part its job

variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Authorize the intended key
pairs.detail: Bind tenant, bucket, prefix, content type, maximum size, checksum algorithm, retention, and expiry before accepting bytes.
pairs.explanation: Bind tenant, bucket, prefix, content type, maximum size, checksum algorithm, retention, and expiry before accepting bytes.

pairs.label: Upload bytes or parts
pairs.detail: Use a unique upload ID, deterministic part numbers, per-part checksums, bounded retries, and a deadline.
pairs.explanation: Use a unique upload ID, deterministic part numbers, per-part checksums, bounded retries, and a deadline. Parts are not yet the published object.

pairs.label: Complete and verify
pairs.detail: Explicitly complete multipart upload, verify final size and checksum, and capture the returned object version or entity tag.
pairs.explanation: Explicitly complete multipart upload, verify final size and checksum, and capture the returned object version or entity tag.

pairs.label: Publish application metadata
pairs.detail: Commit the verified version ID into authoritative application state so readers do not race an ambiguous “latest” object.
pairs.explanation: Commit the verified version ID into authoritative application state so readers do not race an ambiguous “latest” object.

pairs.label: Clean provisional state
pairs.detail: Abort abandoned multipart uploads, quarantine checksum mismatches, and reconcile metadata records whose object commit is unknown.
pairs.explanation: Abort abandoned multipart uploads, quarantine checksum mismatches, and reconcile metadata records whose object commit is unknown.

variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Workload identity
pairs.detail: Use short-lived roles and resource policies scoped to exact operations, buckets, prefixes, encryption keys, network paths, and conditions.
pairs.explanation: Use short-lived roles and resource policies scoped to exact operations, buckets, prefixes, encryption keys, network paths, and conditions.

pairs.label: Signed access
pairs.detail: Pre-signed URLs delegate one method on one key for a short time.
pairs.explanation: Pre-signed URLs delegate one method on one key for a short time. Bind content limits where supported and never expose broad credentials.

pairs.label: Encryption
pairs.detail: Encrypt in transit and at rest, separate key administration, restrict decrypt and grant permissions, and test rotation and recovery.
pairs.explanation: Encrypt in transit and at rest, separate key administration, restrict decrypt and grant permissions, and test rotation and recovery.

pairs.label: Public delivery
pairs.detail: Keep the origin private behind a CDN or controlled gateway, validate cache keys, and prevent untrusted content from executing in a privileged origin.
pairs.explanation: Keep the origin private behind a CDN or controlled gateway, validate cache keys, and prevent untrusted content from executing in a privileged origin.
